design_principles.app_approach: Students meet the decile ladder and the horizon map first — the raw fact — then the decomposition machinery that assigns blame.
Losers become out-of-the-money options; a state toggle shows the beta math (0.05 → −1.44 in a bear rebound) and lets students precompute the crash.
Constant-vol and dynamic weights are two one-line formulas students compute by hand, then see doubling Sharpe ratios across every market.

slides.title: Winners Keep Winning — At One Horizon
slides.content_summary: Definition; ~12%/yr zero-investment; violates weak-form efficiency. The horizon map with real Sharpe bars: reversal <1mo (−0.82), momentum 3–12mo (up to 0.58), reversal 3–5yr (−0.42 to −0.58). Profits dissipate after a year and reverse — a temporary price effect.
slides.lux_integration: Lux: 'Momentum at 12 months and reversal at 60 — can one investor-psychology story produce both?'

slides.title: The Decile Ladder
slides.content_summary: Construction (rank 6–12mo, overlapping 6/6 windows). Real decile returns P1 0.46 → P10 1.63%/mo; 10−1 = 1.17. FF regressions: WML alpha 1.53%/mo (t 5.93); losers load value-like (s 0.51, h 0.38), winners growth-like — the factors push the WRONG way. Momentum becomes Carhart's fourth factor (UMD).
slides.lux_integration: Lux: 'The 3-factor model prices momentum's VARIATION (R² 0.94) but not its MEAN. What does that distinction tell you?'

problem_spec.scenario: The decile table shows a winners-minus-losers spread of 1.17%/month. The FF regression shows a WML three-factor alpha of 1.53%/month.

slides.title: Three Suspects, One Equation
slides.content_summary: E[π] = σμ² + σβ²·Cov(F,F₋₁) + avg own-autocovariance. Factor timing is wrong-signed (market autocovariance < 0); Conrad–Kaul's σμ² needs no predictability; JT's verdict: positive firm-specific autocovariance — delayed reaction to firm news. Skipping a week RAISES profits, against the lead-lag alternative. Ω decomposition: own − cross + dispersion.

slides.title: Moskowitz–Grinblatt: It's (Mostly) Industries
slides.content_summary: Split ε into industry + idiosyncratic. MG Table 1 (real): raw WML 0.43%/mo (t 4.65) collapses to 0.08 (t 0.91) once industry-neutral; industry momentum itself 0.43 (t 4.24); RANDOM industries earn −0.05 (t −1.09). Dispute: Grundy–Martin find both terms positive; Conrad–Kaul rejected by both.
slides.lux_integration: Lux: 'Why is the random-industry row the crucial control?'

slides.title: Your Turn: How Much Is Industry?

problem_spec.scenario: MG Table 1: raw individual-stock momentum earns 0.43%/month; after industry-neutralizing, 0.08%/month remains.

blocks.block_title: Real, Everywhere — and Which Story Fits

slides.title: The Data-Mining Test It Keeps Passing
slides.content_summary: Out-of-sample over time (real numbers): pre-sample 1927–64 mean 0.64 (t 2.60); post-publication 1990–2012 alpha 1.17 (t 3.27) — biggest AFTER fame. Across assets (AMP): positive in every market and class; EW-all Sharpe 0.81 (12.1%/yr); Japan the weak spot (0.12).

slides.title: Risk Says No, Behavior Says Maybe
slides.content_summary: Risk fails on signs: bear markets mkt −4.43 vs WML +1.46; recessions +0.89 — momentum PAYS in bad states. Behavioral: slow diffusion (DHS/BSV/Hong–Stein) + disposition; strongest where news travels slowly — small, low-coverage (concentrated in LOSERS: bad news hides), high-volume, growth. Needs limits to arbitrage. Tension: short-horizon underreaction vs value's long-horizon overreaction.
slides.lux_integration: Lux: 'A strategy that pays +1.46%/mo in bear markets — why is that fatal for a risk-premium story?'

slides.title: Steady Gains, Violent Crashes
slides.content_summary: WML 1927–2010: mean 14.4%, Sharpe 0.52, beta −0.54, alpha 18.4% (t 6.5) — and monthly skew −6.32. Worst months −79/−60/−46/−44/−42%; like a short OTM put. The crash signature: negative 2-yr market + POSITIVE contemporaneous month. 1932: market +82%, losers +236%; 2009: market +29%, losers +156%.
slides.lux_integration: Lux: 'Reconcile Sharpe 0.52 with five months worse than −40%. What moment does the Sharpe ratio ignore?'

slides.title: Losers Become Options
slides.content_summary: 2009 losers (Citi, Ford, GM) down 90%+, levered: equity = OTM call (Merton) ⟹ loser beta spikes to ≈3.7 in the rebound; winner beta ≈1. Regression: normal WML beta 0.05; bear −0.79; bear-and-up a further −0.70. Hedging the rolling beta (Grundy–Martin) removes the 1932 collapse.
slides.lux_integration: Lux: 'Commodities and currencies crash the same way (JFE Table 10) — why is that a problem for the Merton leverage story?'

problem_spec.scenario: DM's regression: WML market beta is 0.05 in normal times, falls by 0.79 in bear markets, and by a further 0.70 when the bear-market month is UP. A bear-market rebound month arrives with the market +10%.
problem_spec.verification: Rebound-state beta = 0.05 − 0.79 − 0.70 = −1.44. Expected WML move ≈ β×market = −1.44×10 = −14.4%.

answers.label: WML beta in the rebound state

slides.title: The Fix: Scale by the Forecast
slides.content_summary: Constant-vol (σtgt/σ̂) vs dynamic (w ∝ μ̂/σ̂² / 2λ). Sharpes 1927–2011: 0.52 → 0.87 → 1.12; dynamic wins every sub-period and every market (Japan 0.07→0.42; all-asset dynamic 1.22); skew flips positive. The crash pattern and the fix replicate in Europe/Japan/UK and in indices, FX, bonds, commodities.

problem_spec.scenario: Target volatility 12%/yr. This month the volatility forecast is σ̂=24%. Separately, the dynamic rule is w = (1/2λ)·μ̂/σ̂² with λ=2, forecast mean μ̂=1%/mo and forecast vol σ̂=5%/mo.

slides.title: One Mechanism, Many Costumes
slides.content_summary: PEAD (CAR drifts by SUE quintile for ~60 days) and earnings momentum (revision drift ~12 months; distinct from price momentum; 34 markets). Disposition effect: sell winners early, ride losers ⟹ underreaction; Frazzini's overhang g=(P−RP)/P — drift 2.1–2.5%/mo when news and overhang align. Hvidkjaer: SMALL trades drive it. Cohen–Frazzini: customer momentum, 4-factor alpha 1.38%/mo (t 3.1); +3.9% on the news, +4.7% drift.
slides.lux_integration: Lux: 'Coastcast's biggest customer fell 30% on public news. Why did Coastcast take WEEKS to react?'

slides.title: Momentum: The Closing Argument
slides.content_summary: Confident: large, monotone, out-of-sample robust; the fourth factor; much is industry momentum; the danger is conditional crash risk. Open: erosion as capital chases it; risk vs behavior; falling transaction costs cut both ways. Investor's job: size to survive the crashes; hedge/scale the time-varying betas.
